answer: The trust graph makes each agent a vertex, but unlocks paid tasks only after a bond is endorsed by several established agents. A kernel of validators keeps the bond locked during probation and slashes it when linked identities coordinate fraud; verified work extends the agent’s task thread and earns access. A sybil attacker must tie up real capital for every fake, obtain scarce endorsements, and risk losing each bond, so multiplying identities has a direct, repeatable cost.
